plan: This is a single-round auction, so there's no learning to be done from previous rounds. My value is $30. I need to consider how Betty and Charles might bid. A simple strategy is to bid slightly below my value, say $29.9. If they bid lower than that, I win and make a profit. If they bid higher, I lose, which is better than winning and losing money. Let's assume they bid their values. I will bid $29.9.

My value is $7. I need to consider how the other bidders, Andy and Charles, will bid. A reasonable strategy is to bid slightly below my value to try and secure a profit if I win. If others bid close to their values, bidding $6.9 might win sometimes and give me a small profit. If others bid lower, I might win with a decent profit. If I bid higher, I risk overpaying. I will bid $6.9.

My value is $36. I want to maximize my profit. If I bid my value, I might win, but I will likely overpay. I should bid less than my value. A good starting point is to bid around 80% of my value. Andy and Betty are unknown. Let's bid $28.80 this round and see what happens. I will adjust my strategy based on the results.
